text: Forty-five dollars in fees. Then two hundred seventy.
You're broke by the twentieth, so you grab a quick loan.
Three hundred dollars until payday. The fee? Just forty-five.
Asked what three months would cost, many guessed just one fee.
So in 2008, researchers changed the cash envelope at 77 payday stores.
It added the fee up. Two weeks, forty-five. Three months, two hundred seventy.
Those borrowers were eleven percent less likely to borrow again.
And they borrowed nearly a quarter less.
A small fee feels like peanuts, until you add it up.
So forty-five dollars? Multiply it first.
